dm_doc.title: Kling 4.0 5-Beat Sheet + Keyframe Prompts
dm_doc.subtitle: Make one 30-second AI shot with a face that stays the same
dm_doc.checked: Kling 4.0 limits checked on 22 November 2026 against Kling's official guides.
intro: Most AI films are short clips glued together, so the face, light and outfit drift at every cut. **Kling 4.0 generates up to 30 seconds in one pass**, and **up to 10 keyframes** plus **up to 15 references** let you plan the whole take like one shot.
This sheet gives you the limits, a 5-beat plan for 30 seconds, copy-paste keyframe prompts and a cheap way to test before you spend credits.

sections.heading: Kling 4.0 limits you plan around

rows: 1-second steps; default 10 s. Kling 3.0 stopped at 15 s.
each one is a moment the video must reach

sections.note: "15 references" is one shared budget, not 15 images plus 15 videos.

sections.heading: The 5-beat sheet (30 seconds)

rows: Who and where: establish the character and the place in one strong image
The character starts doing something; show what they want
Something changes: a reveal, an object, a new person, the weather
The biggest action or emotion of the take
The final state the viewer remembers; end on a clean frame

sections.note: Five keyframes leave room for up to five more if a beat needs a mid-point. Add keyframes only where something changes.

sections.heading: Step by step
checklist: **Write the story in five lines**, one per beat. If a beat needs two sentences, it's two beats — cut something.

**Build a character sheet.** One clean face photo (front, even light) plus 2–4 angles and one full-body shot of the same outfit. Add them as image references and keep the rest of your 15-reference budget for the location or a product.
**Make one keyframe image per beat** with the SAME character and outfit as the references, so the reference and the keyframe never disagree. If they disagree, Kling has to guess which one wins.
**Pick ONE camera move for the whole take** — a slow push-in, a pan or an orbit — and write it in every beat prompt. Changing the move mid-take is what breaks a one-shot look.
**Test cheap first.** Generate only beats 1–2 (about 10 seconds) at 720p. Check the face, outfit and camera. Fix the prompt, then generate the full 30 seconds at 1080p or 4K.
**Keep the audio simple.** One voice profile per character, and say who speaks in which beat.

sections.heading: Copy-paste keyframe prompts
paragraphs: Replace the words in [brackets]. Keep the camera line identical in all five.

**Master prompt:** One continuous 30-second shot, no cuts. [CHARACTER] from @Image1 keeps the same face, hair and outfit in every frame. Location: [PLACE], [TIME OF DAY], [LIGHT]. Camera: one slow [push-in / pan left / orbit] for the whole take. Style: cinematic, natural skin, 9:16.
**Beat 1 (0 s):** Wide shot. [CHARACTER] stands in [PLACE], [ACTION THAT SHOWS WHO THEY ARE]. Calm, establishing.
**Beat 2 (6 s):** [CHARACTER] starts to [GOAL ACTION]; we see what they want. Same light, same outfit.
**Beat 3 (12 s):** [CHANGE] happens — [reveal / object appears / someone enters]. [CHARACTER] reacts with [EMOTION].
**Beat 4 (18 s):** The peak: [BIGGEST ACTION]. Energy rises, camera keeps the same slow move.
**Beat 5 (30 s):** Payoff: [FINAL STATE]. Hold on a clean final frame for 1 second.

**Worked example:** Master — One continuous 30-second shot. A young chai seller from @Image1 in a busy Bengaluru street at golden hour, warm side light; camera: one slow push-in. Beat 1: he pours chai from a height, steam rising. Beat 2: he looks up at a rain cloud and pulls the tarp. Beat 3: rain starts; office workers rush under his stall. Beat 4: he hands out cups to the crowd, laughing. Beat 5: the rain stops, sun breaks through, he raises a cup to the camera.

sections.heading: Mistakes that change the face
bullets: Different outfits in the reference and the keyframes.
Too many people in one take for a first test — start with one character.
A new camera move in every beat.
Spending on 30 seconds before the first two beats look right.
